label: prf:categorical-dq-squared
title: Proof of Non-vanishing of $d_q^2$
html:
Proof. Proof of Non-vanishing of d_q^2

Write a = q^{-1} and b = 1 - q^{-1}, so d_q = ad + b\pi_V d. Then

\begin{align*}
  d_q^2
  &= (ad + b\pi_V d)(ad + b\pi_V d) \\
  &= a^2\underbrace{d^2}_{= 0}
     + ab(d \circ \pi_V d + \pi_V d \circ d)
     + b^2\underbrace{\pi_V d \circ \pi_V d}_{= 0}.
\end{align*}

The first term vanishes because d^2 = 0 in the non-commutative de Rham complex. The last term vanishes because \pi_V is the projection onto the vertical (weight-1) summand of the Reeb decomposition \Omega^k(A) = \Omega^k_H(A) \oplus \varTheta_A \wedge \Omega^{k-1}_H(A): d applied to a vertical form produces one whose vertical component has weight \geq 2 in \varTheta_A, and the contact distribution forces \varTheta_A \wedge \varTheta_A = 0, so \pi_V(d(\pi_V\alpha)) = 0.

For the middle term, the commutator [d, \pi_V] measures how much d fails to preserve the weight grading. On a weight-n form \alpha_n, d\alpha_n = (d\alpha_n)_H + (d\alpha_n)_V, with the weight shift arising from the Lie derivative along \xi (the generator of T):

  [d, \pi_V]\alpha = \mathcal{L}_\xi(\alpha) - \pi_V(\mathcal{L}_\xi(\alpha))
  = \pi_H(\mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha).

Using Cartan's formula \mathcal{L}_\xi = \iota_\xi \circ d + d \circ \iota_\xi and \pi_H + \pi_V = \mathrm{id}, the middle term simplifies to d(\pi_V d\alpha) + \pi_V d(d\alpha) = \omega_V \wedge_q [\xi, \alpha] where \omega_V = d(\pi_V(d1_A)) \in \Omega^2(A) is the curvature of the weight projection --- a canonical 2-form measuring the failure of the horizontal distribution to be integrable. \square
